stanzas: Über ihn, sein Haus und Reich!
Dein Gesetz sei stets sein Wille,
Und vernehm noch an dem Rande
May laurel sprigs blossom for him,
wherever he goes, into a wreath of honour!
Let from the tips of his banners
Pour the fullness of your gifts
over him, his house and realm!
Break the power of wickedness, unmask
May your law always be his will,
and this be to us as laws.
May he joyfully live to see his lands',
See them, one through bonds of brothers,
And may he still hear, at the edge
of a late grave, his grandchildren's chorus:

notes: line 1.1: 'erhalte' = preserve, keep (in life and power); 'Franz' is Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor (from 1804 Francis I of Austria), kept in its German form.
line 1.5: 'Lorbeerreiser' = laurel twigs, the victor's laurels; 'zum Ehrenkranz' = to make a wreath of honour.
line 2.2: 'Furchtbarkeit' = the quality of inspiring fear, terribleness.
line 2.5-6: 'Seiner Hoheit Blitzen' = the lightning (flashes) of His Majesty's power; 'schalten' = rule, hold sway: let his power strike only as justice directs.
line 3.4: 'Schelm- und Bubenstreich' = a rogue's trick and a knave's trick (villainy, treachery), not a harmless prank.
line 3.6: 'Dieser uns Gesetzen gleich' = and may this (his will) be equal to laws for us.
line 4.5-6: 'an dem Rande später Gruft' = at the edge of a late grave, i.e. in a long old age; 'Enkel' = grandchildren, also descendants in general.
